items.quote: carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers
items.party_reason: The NBFC is the designated entity required to carry out periodic updation for medium-risk customers.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Carry out periodic updation of KYC for low-risk customers
items.quote: carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers
items.party_reason: The NBFC is the designated entity responsible for carrying out periodic updation for low-risk customers.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Ensure the updation of KYC for low-risk individual customers within one year of it falling due
items.quote: in respect of an individual customer who is categorised as low-risk, the NBFC shall allow all transactions and ensure the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC
items.trigger: its falling due for KYC
items.party_reason: The NBFC is responsible for ensuring the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for low-risk individual customers.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Ensure the updation of KYC for low-risk individual customers up to the specified date if later than one year after falling due
items.quote: in respect of an individual customer who is categorised as low-risk, the NBFC shall allow all transactions and ensure the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC or up to June 30, 2026, whichever is later
items.party_reason: The NBFC is responsible for ensuring the updation of KYC up to June 30, 2026, or the later date for low-risk individual customers.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Verify the customer's declared new address through positive confirmation
items.quote: In case of a change only in the address details of the customer, the NBFC shall obtain a self-declaration of the new address from the customer through customer’s email-id registered with the NBFC, customer’s mobile number registered with the NBFC, ATMs, digital channels (including mobile application of NBFC), letter, etc., and shall verify the declared address through positive confirmation within two months, by means such as address verification letter, contact point verification, deliverables, etc.
items.trigger: Customer declaring a change in address details
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall obtain a self-declaration and verify the declared address.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Customers must submit the update of documents to the NBFC within 30 days of the update to the documents
items.quote: in case of any update in the documents submitted by the customer at the time of establishment of business relationship / account-based relationship and thereafter, as necessary; customers shall submit to the NBFC the update of such documents. This shall be done within 30 days of the update to the documents for the purpose of updating the records at the NBFC’s end.
items.trigger: update to the documents submitted by the customer
items.party_reason: The text states that customers shall submit the update of documents to the NBFC, placing the duty on the customer rather than the NBFC itself.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
items.obligation: Implement the mechanism for issuing advance intimations and reminders for periodic updation of KYC and recording them in the system for audit trail
items.quote: The NBFC shall expeditiously implement the same but not later than January 01, 2026.
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall expeditiously implement the same but not later than January 01, 2026.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Obligations under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) (UAPA) Act, 1967: > Obligations under Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005 (WMD Act, 2005): | paras 55-56
items.obligation: Forward a copy of application received regarding unfreezing, along with full details of the asset frozen, to the CNO by email, FAX and post
items.quote: Accordingly, the NBFC shall forward a copy of application received from an individual / entity regarding unfreezing, along with full details of the asset frozen, as given by the applicant, to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, within two working days.
items.trigger: receipt of application from an individual / entity regarding unfreezing
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall forward a copy of the application.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Obligations under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) (UAPA) Act, 1967: > Obligations under Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005 (WMD Act, 2005): | paras 55-56
items.obligation: Verify the UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of Designated Individuals and Entities to take into account any modifications and ensure compliance
items.quote:
The NBFC shall verify every day, the ‘UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of

56. Designated Individuals and Entities‘, as available at https://www.mea.gov.in/Implementation-of-UNSC-Sanctions-DPRK.htm, to take into account any modifications to the list in terms of additions, deletions or other changes and also ensure compliance with the ‘Implementation of Security Council Resolution on Democratic People’s Republic of Korea Order, 2017’, as amended from time to time by the Central Government.
items.party_reason: The text states that the NBFC shall verify the sanctions list every day.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information: > Registry (CKYCR) | para 63
items.obligation: Capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR
items.quote: the NBFC shall capture customer’s KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.
items.trigger: commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information: > Registry (CKYCR) | para 63
items.obligation: Furnish updated customer information to CKYCR
items.quote: whenever the NBFC obtains additional or updated information from any customer as per clause (10) below in this paragraph or Rule 9 (1C) of the PML Rules, the NBFC shall within seven days or within such period as may be notified by the Central Government, furnish the updated information to CKYCR
items.trigger: NBFC obtains additional or updated information from any customer as per clause (10) or Rule 9 (1C) of the PML Rules
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall furnish the updated information to CKYCR within seven days.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information: > Wire Transfer | para 69
items.obligation: Review existing agreements or arrangements with unregulated entities involved in wire transfers to ensure compliance with wire transfer information requirements
items.quote: Existing agreements / arrangements, if any, with such entities shall be reviewed within three months to ensure aforementioned requirements.
items.applies_to: NBFCs with existing agreements or arrangements with unregulated entities involved in wire transfers
items.trigger: coming into effect of the directions
items.party_reason: The text states that the concerned NBFC shall review existing agreements or arrangements within three months.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | File No. 14014/01/2019/CFT Government of India Ministry of Home Affairs CTCR Division > affected by the freezing mechanism upon verification that the person or entity is not a designated person: | para 11
items.obligation: Inform and forward a copy of the application together with full details of the asset frozen inadvertently to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA
items.quote: The banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, ROC, Regulators of DNFBPs and the State/ UT Nodal Officers shall inform and forward a copy of the application together with full details of the asset frozen given by any individual or entity informing of the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services have been frozen inadvertently, to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA as per the contact details given in Paragraph 3.1 above, within two working days.
items.applies_to: banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, ROC, Regulators of DNFBPs and the State/ UT Nodal Officers
items.trigger: receipt of an application with evidence that funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services have been frozen inadvertently
items.party_reason: The duty is placed on banks, stock exchanges, depositories, and other listed entities, but not specifically on NBFCs.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | File No. 14014/01/2019/CFT Government of India Ministry of Home Affairs CTCR Division > resources or related services of individuals/organisations in the event of delisting by the UNSCR 1267 (1999), 1988 (2011) and 1989 (2011) Committee | paras 11-12
items.obligation: Forward the delisting application along with full details of the frozen assets to the Central Designated Nodal Officer for UAPA
items.quote: Upon making an application in writing by the concerned individual/organisation, to the concerned bank, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, RoC, Regulators of DNFBPs, Department of Posts and the UAPA Nodal Officers of all States/UTs., who in turn shall forward the application along with the full details of the assets frozen to the Central [Designated] Nodal Officer for UAPA within two working days.
items.applies_to: Concerned bank, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, RoC, Regulators of DNFBPs, Department of Posts, and UAPA Nodal Officers
items.trigger: making an application in writing by the concerned individual/organisation
items.party_reason: The text refers to concerned banks and other regulated entities which include NBFCs forwarding the application.

items.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | F.No.P - 12011/14/2022-ES Cell-DOR Government of India Ministry of Finance Department of Revenue > designated person or no longer meet the criteria for designation: | para 7
items.obligation: Inform and forward a copy of the application, together with full details of the asset frozen, to the CNO by email, FAX and by Post
items.quote: The RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulator and the State Nodal Officer shall inform, and forward a copy of the application, together with full details of the asset frozen, as given by applicant to the CNO by email, FAX and by Post, within two working days.
items.applies_to: RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulator and the State Nodal Officer
items.trigger: receipt of an application with evidence that freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services was inadvertent
items.party_reason: The text lists the RE (Regulated Entity, which includes NBFCs) alongside other bodies as having the duty to inform and forward a copy of the application within two working days.

items.source: Microfinance Institution Directions, 2025 | F. Formation of SRO > Obligations of the SRO towards the Reserve Bank | para 47
items.obligation: Submit its Annual Report to the Reserve Bank
items.quote: The SRO shall submit its Annual Report to the Reserve Bank.
items.party_reason: The duty to submit the Annual Report applies to the SRO (Self-Regulatory Organisation), which is a separate body and not the NBFC.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | A. Regulatory Structure under Scale Based Regulation (SBR) > then would it be still classified in Middle Layer? | paras 19-21
items.obligation: Statutory Auditors are required to certify the asset size (as on March 31) of all the NBFCs in the Group every year and furnish the certificate to the Department of Supervision of the Reserve Bank
items.quote: Statutory Auditors are required to certify the asset size (as on March 31) of all the NBFCs in the Group every year. The certificate shall be furnished to the Department of Supervision of the Reserve Bank under whose jurisdiction the NBFCs are registered.
items.applies_to: all the NBFCs in the Group
items.party_reason: The text states that Statutory Auditors are required to perform the certification and furnish the certificate.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | A.8 Classification in Upper Layer > A.8.2.1 Transition Plan | para 27
items.obligation: Put in place a Board approved policy for adoption of the enhanced regulatory framework and chart out an implementation plan for adhering to the new set of regulations
items.quote: Within three months of being advised by the Reserve Bank regarding its inclusion in the NBFC-UL, the NBFC shall put in place a Board approved policy for adoption of the enhanced regulatory framework and chart out an implementation plan for adhering to the new set of regulations.
items.applies_to: NBFCs identified for inclusion in NBFC-UL
items.trigger: being advised by the Reserve Bank regarding its inclusion in the NBFC-UL
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall put in place a Board approved policy and chart out an implementation plan within three months of being advised.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | A.8 Classification in Upper Layer > A.8.2.1 Transition Plan | para 27
items.obligation: Ensure that the stipulations prescribed for the NBFC-UL are adhered to
items.quote: The Board shall ensure that the stipulations prescribed for the NBFC-UL are adhered to within a maximum time-period of 24 months from the date of advice regarding classification as an NBFC-UL from the Reserve Bank.
items.trigger: date of advice regarding classification as an NBFC-UL from the Reserve Bank
items.party_reason: The Board of the NBFC is explicitly tasked with ensuring the stipulations are adhered to.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | A. Principal Business Criteria > 17[A.1. NBFCs not availing public funds and not having any customer interface | para 38
items.obligation: Existing NBFCs not availing public funds and not having customer interface and meeting the exemption criteria may apply to the Reserve Bank for deregistration
items.quote: Existing ‘NBFCs not availing public funds and not having any customer interface’, including those holding Certificate of Registration as ‘Type I NBFC’, and fulfilling the prescribed criteria for exemption, may apply to the Reserve Bank, for deregistration, within a period of six months i.e., by December 31, 2026.
items.applies_to: Existing NBFCs not availing public funds and not having any customer interface (including Type I NBFCs) fulfilling prescribed criteria for exemption
items.party_reason: The text states that existing NBFCs fulfilling the prescribed criteria may apply to the Reserve Bank for deregistration.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | Chapter-III – Registration requirement > B. Net Owned Fund Requirement | paras 39-42
items.obligation: Achieve intermediate Net Owned Fund (NOF) requirements (₹5 crore for NBFC-ICC, ₹7 crore / ₹5 crore in NE Region for NBFC-MFI, and ₹7 crore for NBFC-Factor) as part of the glide path.
items.quote:
The following glide path is provided for the existing NBFCs, viz., NBFC-ICC, NBFC-MFI (without distinction in the NOF requirement for NBFCs registered in the North East Region) and NBFC-Factor to achieve the NOF of ₹10 crore: |NBFCs|Current NOF|By March 31, 2025|By March 31, 2027| |---|---|---|---| |NBFC-ICC|₹2 crore|₹5 crore|₹10 crore| |NBFC-MFI|₹5 crore
(₹2 crore in NE
Region)|₹7 crore
(₹5 crore in NE
Region)|₹10 crore|
items.party_reason: The existing NBFCs (NBFC-ICC, NBFC-MFI, NBFC-Factor) are responsible for achieving the specified Net Owned Fund requirements along the glide path by the respective deadlines.

items.source: Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation Directions, 2025 | Chapter-IV - Exemptions from the provisions of the RBI Act, 1934 > D. Exemption from sections 45-IA and 45-IC of the RBI Act, 1934 to the following: | para 65
items.obligation: Pass an annual Board Resolution stating that the company will not avail public funds and will not have customer interface during the year
items.quote: It passes an annual Board Resolution at the beginning of the financial year that the company will not avail public funds and will also not have customer interface during the year
items.party_reason: The NBFC itself, through its Board, is required to pass the annual Board Resolution.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter II - Definitions and General Requirements > B. Board approved policies: | para 13
items.obligation: The NBFC must incorporate provisions for resolution under Chapter VI-A into its Board-approved policy.
items.quote:
The board approved policy of the NBFC shall incorporate provisions for resolution as provided for under Chapter VI-A of these Directions, including the following:

(1) the objective principles for the terms of relief to be granted to various borrower / loan categories.

(2) the potential relief measures and the verifiable parameters for making such determination.

4 Inserted with effect from July 1, 2026
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the board approved policy of the NBFC shall incorporate provisions for resolution.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter II - Definitions and General Requirements > C. Early identification and reporting of stress | paras 18-21
items.obligation: Report credit information, including classification of an account as SMA, to the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC) on a monthly basis.
items.quote: A NBFC shall report credit information, including classification of an account as SMA, to Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC), on all borrowers having aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above with them, on a monthly basis.
items.applies_to: all borrowers having aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall report credit information to CRILC on a monthly basis.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter II - Definitions and General Requirements > C. Early identification and reporting of stress | paras 18-21
items.obligation: Submit a weekly report of instances of default by eligible borrowers by close of business on every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday.
items.quote: A NBFC shall submit a weekly report of instances of default by all borrowers (with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above) by close of business on every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday happens to be a holiday.
items.applies_to: all borrowers (with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above)
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall submit a weekly report of instances of default by the specified deadline.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter III - Resolution Process > C. Resolution Plan | paras 44-47
items.obligation: Implement the resolution plan
items.quote: In respect of accounts with aggregate exposure above a specified threshold with the specified lenders on or after the ‘reference date’, resolution plan shall be implemented within 180 days from the end of Review Period
items.applies_to: accounts with aggregate exposure above a specified threshold with the specified lenders on or after the ‘reference date’
items.trigger: the end of Review Period
items.party_reason: The resolution plan must be implemented by the specified lenders, which include NBFCs.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter VI - Special Cases of Restructuring > C. Compromise Settlements and Technical Write-offs | paras 93-94
items.obligation: Report compromise settlements and technical write-offs approved by a particular authority to the next higher authority
items.quote: There shall be a reporting mechanism to the next higher authority, at least on a quarterly basis, with respect to compromise settlements and technical write offs approved by a particular authority.
items.party_reason: The reporting mechanism for compromise settlements and technical write-offs applies to the NBFC's internal authorities and management.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | E. Projects Under Implementation > the original DCCO | paras 111-113
items.obligation: Meet all specified conditions (completion of documentation/security creation and reflecting capital structure/financing agreement changes in books) in respect of all lenders for successful implementation of a resolution plan
items.trigger: the end of the Review Period
items.party_reason: The conditions apply to all lenders, which includes NBFCs acting as lenders in the resolution plan.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter VI - Special Cases of Restructuring > A. Implementation of Resolution Plan by the NBFCs | para 122
items.obligation: Invoke resolution under this Chapter no later than 45 days from the date of calamity declaration
items.quote: Resolution under this Chapter shall be invoked no later than 45 days from the date of the declaration of calamity
items.trigger: date of the declaration of calamity
items.party_reason: The text discusses resolution implementation and invocation duties applicable to the NBFC under these Directions.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter VI - Special Cases of Restructuring > A. Implementation of Resolution Plan by the NBFCs | para 122
items.obligation: Implement resolution under this Chapter within 135 days from the date of calamity declaration
items.quote: shall be implemented within 135 days from the date of the declaration.
items.trigger: date of the declaration of calamity
items.party_reason: The NBFC is the regulated entity responsible for implementing the resolution plan within the specified timeframe.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter VI - Special Cases of Restructuring > C. Reporting Requirements | para 122
items.obligation: Upload the data on relief measures on the CIMS portal within 30 days from the end of the half-year
items.quote: NBFC shall upload the data on relief measures on a half-yearly basis within 30 days from the end of the half-year (September 30thand March 31stof every year) on the CIMS portal.
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall upload the data on relief measures on the CIMS portal within 30 days.

items.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter XI - General Principles and Prudential Norms for Restructured Advances > A. General instructions for restructuring of advances | paras 178-183
items.obligation: Implement a restructuring package
items.quote: A restructuring package shall be implemented within 120 days from the date of receipt of application by the NBFC.
items.trigger: receipt of application by the NBFC
items.party_reason: The text states the restructuring package application is received by the NBFC and must be implemented within 120 days.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | A. Fair Practices Code for NBFCs > A.4 General | paras 18-20
items.obligation: Convey consent or objection to a borrower's request for transfer of borrowal account
items.quote: In case of receipt of request from the borrower for transfer of borrowal account, the consent or otherwise i.e., objection of the NBFC, if any, shall be conveyed within 21 days from the date of receipt of request.
items.trigger: receipt of request from the borrower for transfer of borrowal account
items.party_reason: The text explicitly mentions that the objection or consent of the NBFC shall be conveyed within 21 days.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct > D. Reset of Floating Interest Rate on Equated Monthly Instalments (EMI) based Personal Loans | para 31
items.obligation: Share or make accessible to borrowers a statement enumerating principal and interest recovered till date, EMI amount, number of EMIs left, and annualized rate of interest/APR for the entire tenor of the loan
items.quote: An NBFC shall share / make accessible to the borrowers, through appropriate channels, a statement at the end of each quarter which shall at the minimum, enumerate the principal and interest recovered till date, EMI amount, number of EMIs left and annualized rate of interest / APR for the entire tenor of the loan.
items.applies_to: Floating interest rate EMI based Personal Loans
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall share or make accessible the statement to the borrowers.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | F. Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents on Repayment / Settlement of Personal Loans > F.1 Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents | paras 35-38
items.obligation: Release all original movable / immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry
items.quote: An NBFC shall release all the original movable / immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan account.
items.trigger: full repayment/ settlement of the loan account
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall release the property documents and remove charges within 30 days.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | F. Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents on Repayment / Settlement of Personal Loans > F.2 Compensation for delay in release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents | paras 39-41
items.obligation: Communicate to the borrower reasons for delay in releasing original movable/immovable property documents or failing to file charge satisfaction form with relevant registry beyond 30 days after loan repayment/settlement
items.quote: An NBFC shall communicate to the borrower reasons for delay in releasing of original movable / immovable property documents or failing to file charge satisfaction form with relevant registry beyond 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of loan.
items.trigger: full repayment/ settlement of loan
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall communicate to the borrower reasons for delay.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | F. Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents on Repayment / Settlement of Personal Loans > F.2 Compensation for delay in release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents | paras 39-41
items.obligation: Complete the procedure to assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate/certified copies of lost or damaged property documents within an additional 30 days (total period of 60 days) before delay penalty applies
items.quote: However, in such cases, an additional time of 30 days will be available to the NBFC to complete this procedure and the delayed period penalty will be calculated thereafter (i.e., after a total period of 60 days).
items.applies_to: Personal loans with loss/damage to original property documents
items.trigger: full repayment/ settlement of loan where there is loss/damage to original property documents
items.party_reason: The text assigns the timeframe and completion of the procedure directly to the NBFC.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.5 Release of Collateral after Repayment | paras 58-59
items.obligation: Release or return pledged eligible collateral held as security to the borrower(s) or legal heir(s)
items.quote: An NBFC shall release or return the pledged eligible collateral held as security to the borrower(s)/ legal heir(s) on the same day but in any case, not exceeding a maximum period of seven working days upon full repayment or settlement of the loan.
items.applies_to: NBFCs lending against gold and silver collateral
items.trigger: full repayment or settlement of the loan
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC shall release or return the pledged eligible collateral.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.6 Transparency in Auction Procedure | paras 63-66
items.obligation: Refund surplus, if any, from the auction of gold or silver collateral to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s)
items.quote: The surplus, if any, from the auction of the gold or silver collateral, shall be refunded to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within a maximum period of seven working days from the date of receipt of the full auction proceeds.
items.applies_to: NBFCs lending against gold and silver collateral
items.trigger: receipt of the full auction proceeds
items.party_reason: The NBFC is responsible for refunding the surplus from the auction to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within the stipulated timeframe.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral > G.8 Unclaimed Gold and Silver collateral | paras 71-72
items.obligation: Put up a report on unclaimed gold and/or silver collateral to the Customer Service Committee or the Board for a review
items.quote: A report on unclaimed gold and /or silver collateral shall be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, as the case may be, at half-yearly intervals for a review.
items.applies_to: NBFCs lending against gold and silver collateral
items.party_reason: The report on unclaimed gold and/or silver collateral must be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board of the NBFC.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Chapter IV – Miscellaneous > A. Need for public notice before closure of the branch/office | para 102
items.obligation: Give public notice in at least one leading national newspaper and a leading local vernacular newspaper indicating the purpose and arrangements being made to service depositors prior to the closure of any branch or office.
items.quote: The NBFC shall give at least three months public notice prior to the date of closure of any of its branches/offices in, at least, one leading national newspaper and a leading local (covering the place of branch / office) vernacular newspaper indicating therein the purpose and arrangements being made to service the depositors, etc.
items.trigger: date of closure of any of its branches/offices
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that the NBFC shall give the public notice prior to closing a branch or office.

items.source: Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025 | Part 2 (Other qualitative information) | para 109
items.obligation: Ensure a response is made within 1 working day if a generic email ID is furnished for the nodal grievance redressal officer
items.quote: An NBFC may furnish generic email id, provided a response is made within 1 working day
items.applies_to: NBFCs furnishing a generic email id for the nodal grievance redressal officer
items.trigger: receipt of an email/query at the generic email ID
items.party_reason: The text explicitly states that an NBFC may furnish a generic email id provided a response is made within 1 working day, placing the responsibility on the NBFC.
